title: ZFS DMU userspace object API
description:
Define and implement a stable userspace interface to the OpenZFS Data Management Unit (DMU) object store layer. This is the prerequisite for the ZFS DMU block store backend.

## Why ZFS DMU

The DMU is ZFS's internal content-aware block storage layer. It already does what usenet-ipfs needs: immutable block storage, per-block checksums (SHA-256 or SHA-512), native deduplication, copy-on-write, and snapshots. Mapping CIDs to DMU objects is natural — the checksum ZFS computes is the same hash we already use for CIDs.

## The problem

OpenZFS does not expose a stable, documented userspace API for raw DMU object operations (alloc, write, read, free by object ID). Existing userspace interfaces are management-plane only (libzfs, libzfs_core, zfs_ioctl) and not designed for data-path use.

## What needs doing

Evaluate and prototype one or more of the following approaches, then select and implement one:

- **ioctl-based**: extend or wrap the existing `zfs_ioctl` interface; stable but requires root or delegated permissions and kernel module cooperation
- **FUSE dataset bridge**: mount a ZFS dataset via FUSE and expose a custom object-ID → bytes API over a UNIX socket; avoids kernel changes but adds a daemon hop
- **Kernel module shim**: thin kernel module that exposes a /dev interface for DMU object alloc/read/write/free; most direct but requires kernel module maintenance across ZFS versions
- **zvol + custom layout**: use a ZFS zvol as a raw block device and implement a minimal object index on top; avoids DMU API problem entirely but loses native dedup and checksumming

The chosen approach must provide:
- `object_write(data: &[u8]) -> ObjectId` — allocate a new object and write bytes
- `object_read(id: ObjectId) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` — read object by ID
- `object_exists(id: ObjectId) -> bool`
- A stable Rust FFI or socket-based client crate (`usenet-ipfs-zfs-dmu`)

## Acceptance criteria
- Rust crate compiles on Linux with OpenZFS installed
- Round-trip test: write bytes, read back, assert match
- Works without root if possible; documents privilege requirements if not
- Benchmarked against filesystem and Kubo backends (latency and throughput)
